resources.string: Traffic from HERE, TomTom or both, with your own API keys, while a route is being followed. With this off, live traffic makes no network connection.

Asks the chosen provider for traffic on the road ahead while a route is followed on the car\'s screen, to colour the route, add the delay to the arrival time and offer a faster way round. It needs your own key for the chosen provider, saved below, before it can be turned on. The first time you turn it on, the phone shows exactly what it sends. Off, nothing is sent and nothing connects.
Which service to ask. With both, the first named is preferred: its flow colours the route.

Combined asks both every refresh: flow from the preferred one, incidents and closures from both, so it uses both allowances. Failover asks the second only when the first has no key, is at its limit or fails.

While a route is being followed, every 10 minutes (or as set), the rectangle around the next 30 km of the route, and your key, to each provider chosen above. That shows the provider roughly where you are. Each provider also sees your IP address and when you asked. None receives your destination or the route itself.
HERE\'s End User Terms: https://legal.here.com/us-en/terms/here-end-user-terms\nHERE\'s Privacy Policy: https://legal.here.com/us-en/privacy
TomTom\'s legal terms: https://developer.tomtom.com/legal\nTomTom\'s Privacy Policy: https://www.tomtom.com/privacy/

Your own key from HERE\'s platform account. It is kept only in this app\'s private storage on the phone, never backed up and never shown again once saved, and is sent only to HERE with each request. HERE bills the key\'s owner for use above its free allowance.

Your own key from TomTom\'s developer portal. It is kept only in this app\'s private storage on the phone, never backed up and never shown again once saved, and is sent only to TomTom with each request. TomTom bills the key\'s owner for use above its free allowance.
No key saved. Save one to turn live traffic on.
That is not a key: it is empty, or has spaces in it.

Makes one request to each chosen provider with a key, for incidents in a small fixed area of downtown Dallas that says nothing about where you are, and shows \"works\" or the provider\'s own error. It counts towards the monthly limits. Only with live traffic on.

How often to ask again while a route is followed, and once more after a re-route. For HERE each time is two requests: flow and incidents, so at 10 minutes, two hours of driving a day is about 720 requests a month. For TomTom each time is one incidents request plus about 15 to 40 flow tiles.
How much of the route ahead to ask about. Each provider is sent the rectangle around that much of the route, so a longer look ahead shows it a larger area and costs more mobile data.

When this many requests have been made this month, HERE is not asked until the 1st of next month and this card says so. HERE\'s free allowance is 5,000 a month; after that it charges the key\'s owner. The count is kept on the phone, as numbers only.
Not saved: enter a number from 2 to 1,000,000.

When this many incident requests have been made this month, TomTom is not asked until the 1st of next month. TomTom\'s free allowance is 2,500 a month. Flow tiles are counted separately and capped at 180,000 a month, under TomTom\'s 200,000.
Not saved: enter a number from 1 to 1,000,000.
Debug build: requests go to the lab\'s stand-in server %1$s, not to HERE or TomTom.
